background_notes.justification: A positive integer maps to a complex number with that same positive real part, so it cannot be zero; a nonzero negative integer is the negative of a positive one. background_notes.fact: For a finite basis (e_i) of a complex vector space, every w has unique coefficients q_i with w=∑q_i e_i. If h is complex-linear, h e_i=a_i e_i, and h w=bw, then q_i(a_i−b)=0 for every i. If all a_i−b are nonzero, then w=0.
